learningObjective: Explain why the three Q, K, V linear projections are fused into a single GEMM and what the correctness and performance requirements are.
stem: A transformer implementation replaces three separate linear projections (X@W_Q, X@W_K, X@W_V) with a single fused GEMM X @ [W_Q | W_K | W_V] whose output is sliced into Q, K, V. Which characterization is correct?

options.text: Fusing the three projections produces different Q, K, V values compared to separate projections because the shared reduction accumulator introduces cross-projection numerical coupling; the fusion must be disabled whenever bit-exact reproducibility of separate projections is required.
Fused QKV is only safe when H_kv = H (i.e., MHA); MQA and GQA break the fusion because Q has H heads while K, V have H_kv < H heads, so the concatenated weight matrix is no longer rectangular.

The fusion doubles compute FLOPs because the combined weight matrix is [D, 3D] rather than [D, D], turning the projection into a wider GEMM whose runtime is bounded by tensor-core issue rate rather than memory.

Numerically the fused and separate projections are equivalent (up to rounding order). The primary benefit is a single kernel launch and one HBM read of X instead of three; the concatenation of the weight matrices is done offline so W is fetched once for the combined GEMM.

explanation: Concatenating [W_Q | W_K | W_V] into a single [D, 3D] weight matrix and computing X @ W in one GEMM produces the same numerical result as three separate GEMMs (up to summation order rounding). The wins are: one kernel launch (amortizes launch overhead), one HBM read of X (activation is reused across all three output slices), and better tensor-core utilization on a wider GEMM. FLOPs are unchanged. MQA/GQA are handled by concatenating a rectangular [D, D + 2*H_kv*d_head] matrix.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: no cross-projection coupling; each output column is an independent dot product.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: MQA/GQA just concatenate a differently-shaped rectangular matrix.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: FLOPs are 2 * B*N*D*3D total either way (sum of three separate GEMMs = one wide GEMM).

assumptions: Weights are stored contiguously as a single [D, 3D] (or [D, D + 2*H_kv*d]) tensor.
The output is contiguous and can be sliced without copies.
nonImplications: Does not imply the fused kernel is always faster; on very small B*N, launch overhead is not the bottleneck.
Does not imply that a fused kernel must also fuse the RoPE / bias-add / attention itself.

sourceRefs.locator: GEMM launch amortization and shared-input reuse
